evals.name: immersive-3d-hero
evals.prompt: Build a landing page hero section for 'Driftline', a developer-tools SaaS. I want an immersive dark-theme 3D hero: a particle field that drifts and reacts to the mouse, with the headline 'Ship faster than gravity' and a CTA over it. As you scroll into the next section the particles should morph or scatter with the scroll. Stack: React + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind. It has to feel award-winning, not templated, and stay smooth on mid-range devices. Set up the project from scratch and make sure it builds.
evals.expected_output: A Vite React TS project with an R3F particle hero: shader-driven particles, mouse + scroll reactivity via a single scroll source, DPR cap, reduced-motion and WebGL fallbacks, clean build.
assertions: build-passes: tsc --noEmit and npm run build both completed with 0 errors
uses-r3f-not-raw-renderer: @react-three/fiber is used; no hand-rolled WebGLRenderer in React components
dpr-capped: Canvas caps device pixel ratio at 2 or below
no-setstate-in-useframe: per-frame animation mutates refs/uniforms, never React state
particles-animated-on-gpu: particle motion in the vertex shader, not per-frame JS buffer writes
single-scroll-source: one scroll system drives the scene
reduced-motion-handled: prefers-reduced-motion produces a static/minimal experience
webgl-fallback: styled static fallback when WebGL is unavailable

evals.name: shader-hover-grid
evals.prompt: I have a portfolio site idea: a project grid where each project image gets a WebGL hover effect (ripple/RGB-shift distortion, the kind you see on Awwwards sites), images otherwise laid out as a normal responsive grid. Also add a full-screen scroll-driven 3D section above the grid where a simple abstract object rotates and the camera pushes in as you scroll. React + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind. Use placeholder images. Build it from scratch and verify it compiles.
evals.expected_output: A Vite React TS project with DOM-synced shader planes over a real image grid (cover-fit UVs, eased hover uniform), plus a ScrollTrigger-driven 3D section, fallbacks, clean build.
assertions: build-passes: tsc --noEmit and npm run build both completed with 0 errors
dpr-capped: every Canvas caps device pixel ratio at 2 or below
cover-fit-uvs: image shader corrects plane-vs-image aspect so images are not stretched
eased-hover-uniform: hover uniform eased over time, not snapped
no-setstate-in-useframe: per-frame animation mutates refs/uniforms, never React state
single-scroll-source: one scroll system drives the 3D section
reduced-motion-handled: prefers-reduced-motion produces a static/minimal experience
dom-grid-integrity: grid stays a real DOM layout that works without WebGL
